Repaint threat overlay (paint_threat_overlay_for_team 0 then 1). spawn=desired; if chapter_init_phase_flag==0 scan tile map (height*width tiles, attr byte at stride*4+6) for the nearest walkable+unoccupied tile (bit 0x40 clear) by taxicab |dx|+|dy| from desired, taking that as spawn. Call fd2_obfuscate_battle_tile_map. pRec = tile_event_data_table + char_field_idx*0x1a + 0x83: team=pRec[0], char_id=pRec[1], level=pRec[4]. If char_id<0x44 (player class): base=fd2_get_char_base_entry, growth=fd2_get_char_growth_entry; HP=base[3]+growth[6]*(level-1), MP=base[5]+growth[8]*(level-1), AP=base[0x12]+growth[0]*level, DP=base[0x14]+growth[2]*level, DX=base[0x16]+growth[4]*level, magic_resist=base[7], slot+0x1f/+0x20=base[0]/base[1]. Else (enemy, char_id>=0x44): enemy=fd2_get_enemy_data_entry(char_id-0x44); HP=level*enemy_word[2], MP=level*enemy[4], AP=level*enemy[5], DP=level*enemy[6], DX=level*enemy[7], magic_resist=enemy[8], slot+0x1f/+0x20=enemy[0]/enemy[1]. Populate slot: pos x/y from spawn; sprite_state[0]=fd2_load_portrait_to_cache(char_id,fdicon_fp), [1..3]=0; team; char_id (twice, +7/+8); equip-slot encoding from pRec[5]/[6] (pRec[5]==0xFF -> second-slot-only mask 0x80, else dual 0x40/0x40); 6 inventory item IDs+flags from pRec[7..0xc] (-1 -> flag 0x80); status bytes +0x22..+0x27 zeroed; spell bitmap memmove pRec+0xd (4 bytes) to slot+0x1a; +0x21=level; pickup kind pRec[0x16]->+0x31; pickup param ushort pRec[0x17]->+0x32; AI overrides pRec[0x11..0x13]->+0x34..+0x36; ai_target_id pRec[2]->+0x3d; movement_order +0x3c = 0 if team==2 (player) else 0xFF; HP_cur=HP_max=HP (+0x40/+0x42), MP_cur=MP_max=MP (+0x44/+0x46). fd2_recalculate_combat_stats(party_member_count); party_member_count++.

The +4/+6 writes intentionally land in the next tile's 4-byte record (vendor stride design; see fd2_obfuscate_battle_tile_map for map layout).

If filled_count>0: blits sprite 0x17 (left cap) at dst; sprite 0x18 (filled middle) at dst+1..dst+(filled_count-1); sprite 0x19 (fill right cap) at dst+filled_count. If filled_count>0x45 returns early (exceeds max width, no final cap). Otherwise fills remaining positions filled_count+1..0x45 with sprite 0x1D (empty middle), then falls through to one trailing sprite 0x1E (final right cap). Both terminal paths (empty-bar loop exit and filled-bar empty-middle loop break) share the same trailing 0x1E blit using the last computed seg_addr (asm: shared EAX held across the merge near 0x1E7DF). Accurately describes a sparse delta chunk handler that reads N (offset, run_length, fill_byte) records and run-fills each at base+offset (REP STOSW + trailing STOSB == memset of run_length bytes). No Ghidra address residue; 'byte' = element size semantics (vs sibling chunk_sparse_copy_literal which copies literal bytes; vs chunk_sparse_set_byte which sets a single byte per offset).
00036c2c.purpose: ANI frame-decoder dispatch handler (table slot 8 @ 0x5278A): applies N sparse run-fills, each writing run_length copies of a fill byte at base+offset within the destination row buffer.
00036c2c.logic_summary: Reads ushort N from the shared stream cursor. base = dst_buf (data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_dst_buf @ 0x52762). Loops N times: read ushort offset, byte run_length, byte fill; memset(base+offset, fill, run_length). In the binary this is REP STOSW of run_length>>1 broadcast words plus a trailing STOSB when run_length is odd (== run_length bytes total). Cursor advances 2 + 4*N bytes; void return; no stack args (custom ESI register protocol, modeled in C by file-scope g_ani_cursor).

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect: writes run-filled bytes into the destination row buffer and advances the shared stream cursor by 2 + 4*N bytes.

reads_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-scope shared stream cursor modeling ESI)
00036c2c.notes: Disassembly (0x36c2c) confirms: LODSW N; EBX=[0x52762] dst_buf; per record EDI=base+offset, CL=run_length, AL/AH=fill broadcast, SHR ECX,1 + REP STOSW + RCL ECX,1 + REP STOSB == memset(base+offset, fill, run_length); DEC EDX loop. Invoked only indirectly via dispatch table slot @0x5278A (xref to fn is DATA from 0005278a; get_function_callers empty as expected). Caller chain: fd2_ani_decoder_decode_frame_bytes @0x36C9E dispatches by opcode byte. src comment (anidec.c lines 244-249) already concise and correct; Ghidra plate detailed and consistent -> no edits. Byte read order (length at lower addr, fill at higher addr) matches src's two sequential g_ani_cursor reads. No logic/equivalence concerns.

00036c56.name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=ani_decoder/animation). Descriptor 'sparse_copy_literal' accurately captures behavior: sparse=offset-addressed segments, copy=memcpy of stream bytes, literal=raw uncompressed bytes. Parallels well-formed siblings fd2_ani_decoder_chunk_sparse_set_byte / sparse_set_run_byte. No Ghidra address residue.
00036c56.purpose: ANI delta-stream chunk handler: applies N sparse literal-copy segments {offset, length, literal bytes} into the current row destination buffer (each segment memcpy'd to dst_buf + offset).
00036c56.logic_summary: Reads ushort N = segment count, then loops N times. Each iteration: reads ushort offset, byte length, then memcpy's 'length' literal bytes from the stream cursor to dst_buf + offset. In the binary the copy is the Watcom inlined memcpy idiom (SHR ECX,1; REP MOVSW; RCL ECX,1; REP MOVSB = word copy + odd-byte tail). dst pointer is reset from EBX (=dst_buf base) each iteration; the cursor advances by 2 + sum_i(3 + length_i). No return value.

returns.semantics: none (writes decoded literal bytes into the row destination buffer; advances the shared stream cursor)

reads_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-static stream cursor; C analog of the binary's ESI)
writes_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-static stream cursor advanced past the consumed segments)
00036c56.notes: Disasm (LODSW count; per-segment LODSW offset / LODSB length / REP MOVSW+MOVSB copy; DEC EDX loop) and decompilation both match the C source at anidec.c lines 277-295 exactly; faithful equivalence-preserving translation. Invoked indirectly via dispatch table slot @ 0x5278E (frame dispatch table @ 0x5276A), so get_function_callers reports none and the only xref is DATA from 0x5278E -- expected. Binary uses ESI as the stream cursor; the C version uses file-static g_ani_cursor (documented at anidec.c header lines 6-8), an intentional translation, not a logic change. 00036c9e.name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=ani_decoder, descriptor=decode_frame_bytes). No address residue. Accurately reflects purpose: the top-level loop that decodes one ANI frame's chunk-byte stream by dispatching each chunk-type byte to the handler table.
00036c9e.purpose: Top-level ANI.DAT frame decoder loop: walks a frame's chunk-byte stream, dispatching each chunk-type byte through the 10-entry handler table so the handlers apply the frame's delta to the target buffer.
00036c9e.logic_summary: EBP frame (saves EBX/ESI/EDI), no __CHK. If chunk_count==0 returns immediately. Sets the shared cursor g_ani_cursor = src_buf_ptr ONCE (binary: MOV ESI,[EBP+0xC] at 0x36CAF, outside the loop). Loop body: read one chunk-type byte via *g_ani_cursor++ (binary LODSB), index data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_frame_dispatch_table[chunk_type] (binary SUB AH,AH / SHL AX,2 / MOVZX EBX,AX / CALL [EBX+0x5276A]), call the zero-arg void handler, then chunk_count--. Only the chunk-type byte is consumed here; each handler advances the SAME g_ani_cursor by its own operand bytes, so the cursor walks the entire stream cooperatively. The Ghidra decompile models the cursor as a per-call local (stream_ptr+1) which loses the shared-cursor semantics; the source's file-scope g_ani_cursor is the correct model (handlers consume variable amounts from the same cursor). Disassembly confirms loop re-enters at LODSB (0x36CB2), not at the MOV ESI reload.

params.reason: Describes the input stream pointer; no address residue. (Ghidra types it byte*; source uses uint32 cast to uint8* -- representation choice only, types are out of scope to change.)

returns.semantics: No return value; side effect is the decoded frame written to the target buffer via the dispatched handlers.

issues.title: Dispatch table indexed by full byte (0-255) but emitted as a 10-entry array
issues.description: chunk_type is a uint8 (0-255) used to index data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_frame_dispatch_table, which the Layer-2 port declares as [10] (src/table/anitab.c, src/include/globals.h). The original binary's table at 0x5276A is also exactly 10 pointers (verified: the 10th pointer ends at 0x52792, followed by 4 zero bytes then the 'Stack Overflow!' literal -- not an 11th entry). So both binary and port assume well-formed ANI.DAT streams emit only opcodes 0-9; a malformed byte >= 10 would read past the array in both. This is faithful to the original (not a port-introduced regression) and ANI.DAT is a trusted bundled asset, so it is informational only -- no change in this stage.
issues.evidence: Decoder: src/anim/anidec.c L74-77 indexes table[chunk_type] with chunk_type from *g_ani_cursor++. Table decl: src/include/globals.h L527 'extern void (*...frame_dispatch_table[10])(void);' and src/table/anitab.c L480. Binary extent: read_memory(0x52792,48) = 00 00 00 00 'Stack Overflow!\r\n' confirming exactly 10 entries; first entries 0x36AE7,0x36B01,... match handler addresses.

issues.title: Table extent (30) is shorter than the full spell-id index space (max 0x23=35)
issues.description: Spell IDs reach 0x23 (35), but the table is 30 bytes (indices 0..29) and the reader copies exactly 30 bytes into a 32-byte stack scratch. For spell_id >= 30 (sword skill 音速刃 0x1E=30 and summons 0x20-0x23) the indexed byte load reads beyond the 30 copied bytes (into the upper, uninitialised slots of the 32-byte local). This is the vendor binary's own behaviour, faithfully reproduced: the C array holds the exact 30 vendor bytes and the reader copies exactly 30 as the original does, so it is NOT a rebuild equivalence bug. 00060003.purpose: VGA palette-cycle RGB animation source for environment effects (water/lava/fire): the 16-frame sliding-window RGB stream that fd2_update_palette_cycle_anim scrolls through palette indices 0xE0..0xEF.
00060003.logic_summary: Flat read-only uint8 stream of 31 contiguous 3-byte RGB triples (93 bytes). Sole accessor fd2_update_palette_cycle_anim @ 0x4DFCC computes frame_idx(0..15)*3 (MOV AH,3 / MUL AH @ 0x4DFFD-0x4DFFF), LEAs the table base (0x4E001, DATA xref), adds the offset (ADD ESI,EAX @ 0x4E007), then loops 16 colors (MOV ECX,0x10 @ 0x4E009) emitting 3 LODSB bytes per color to the VGA DAC data port 0x3C9 (LODSB @ 0x4E019, READ xref). Each frame f reads the sliding 48-byte window [f*3 .. f*3+47]; max start 15*3=45, +48 -> last byte 92 -> exactly 93 bytes. Adjacent frames share 15 of 16 triples, producing a smooth scrolling palette animation. Components are 6-bit VGA values (0..0x3F).
00060003.element_semantics: One unsigned 8-bit VGA DAC color component (6-bit range 0..0x3F). Bytes are grouped as 31 consecutive RGB triples (R,G,B); they are consumed as an overlapping sliding window rather than as fixed per-frame rows. Index into the stream = frame_idx*3 + intra-frame byte position.

00014625.purpose: Mark a '+' shaped 5-tile AoE/threat overlay pattern centered at (x,y) on the battle tile map: center tile gets overlay bit 0x40, the four cardinal neighbors get bit 0x80.

(Watcom __CHK(0x14) stack-probe in the binary is elided in the rebuilt C source per project convention.)

00021eb1.logic_summary: Computes cursor pixel center (cursor_screen_x*0x18+0xC, cursor_screen_y*0x18+0x10). malloc(0x25680) snapshot buffer and composites the current battle tile map into it at +0x8088 (stride 0x1C8, tile 0xD x 8 at the battle view-window origin). Picks the spotlight char (the enemy-side combatant: if attacker.team==0 the attacker, else the defender) and the terrain char (the other). Derives a terrain BG byte from the under-foot tile attribute (tile_attr[6]), except for immune classes (job==0x13 or archetype in {4,5}) with portrait!=0x1C, where the per-chapter override byte data_fd2_chapter_combat_cinematic_mode_per_chapter[chapter] is used when non-zero. In scripted mode forces spotlight_terrain and banner_idx to the scripted value, and banner_idx to 3 for climactic portraits (attacker 0x1A/0x36 or defender 0x37). Loads the defender counter-blow FIGANI only when counter-eligible or scripted. Sequence: fade to black, flash attacker silhouette (non-scripted), zoom the pose in, run the attacker hit cinematic; if it landed and the defender can counter (non-scripted) run the swapped counter cinematic; in scripted mode latch the flag to 1 and run the counter cinematic. Cleanup: frees all scratch + loaded resources (split-bg B + 3 sub-layers only when split); when non-scripted reallocates the large game-state buffer, reloads the battle-scene snapshot from FDSHAP.DAT, restores the portrait cache, settles 6 ticks, fades to black, clears VGA, recomposites the battle frame, stops the FIGANI SFX, frees both SFX banks, fades in.

0002935b.name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=blit/gfx, descriptor=indexed_sprite). Accurately describes the body: it indexes sprite #sprite_idx via the sheet's 4-byte-per-entry offset table and dispatches the decode+paint. No Ghidra address residue. Canonical, cleanest-named member of the indexed-sprite blit family (the sibling fd2_blit_indexed_sprite_at_xy carries a misleading legacy name, but this one is accurate); ~30 callers across battle/event/cinematic rendering.
0002935b.purpose: Indexed-sprite blit dispatcher: looks up sprite #sprite_idx in a sprite-atlas sheet's offset table and forwards the actual RLE decode + paint to fd2_rle_blit_sprite.
0002935b.logic_summary: sprite_data = sheet_ptr + *(int32*)(sheet_ptr + 8 + sprite_idx*4); then fd2_rle_blit_sprite(sprite_data+9, width=*(uint16*)sprite_data, height=*(uint16*)(sprite_data+2), dst_buf, dst_stride, palette_op). The sheet's offset table base is sheet_ptr+8 (vs +6 in the sibling _at_offset/_at_xy variants) and the RLE stream begins 9 bytes into each sprite data block (after the 4-byte width/height header + 5 reserved bytes). Loop tail: defender HP==0 forces hit_count=0; while positive and attacker_figani[+1]==1 the attacker recoil + opposite-direction zoom replays for the second strike. 0002f8ea.purpose: Chapter-intro menu action that gives/trades one item from a source party member's inventory to a target party member.
0002f8ea.logic_summary: Infinite do/while loop. (3) If the list is empty, set last_action_sprite_id_param = source.char_id+1, show the 'nothing to give' reject dialog (page 0x1FF) and loop back. (4) Reset cursor/scroll, open the sell-mode item panel (sell_mode=1 is layout-only) and run fd2_shop_menu_input_loop to pick the item; Esc loops back. (5) Show the 'give to whom?' informational dialog (page 0x1FE, not a yes/no confirm), then run the roster select again to pick the TARGET member; Esc loops back. (6) If the target already holds 8 items (fd2_count_usable_inventory_slots==8), set last_action_sprite_id_param = target.char_id+1 and show the per-chapter 'inventory full' reject dialog (data_fd2_dialog_shop_inventory_full_dialog_text_id_table[cursor_state]) and loop back; otherwise re-fetch the item id from the source slot (fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id), remove it from the source (fd2_remove_inventory_slot_at), add it unequipped to the target (fd2_add_item_to_inventory), and recompute only the SOURCE's combat stats (fd2_recalculate_combat_stats). The shop cursor indexes the compacted display list but is reused directly as a raw slot index, which is correct because inventories are kept gap-free.

issues.title: Out-of-bounds frame read when terrain class exceeds the 5-entry table
issues.description: The handler indexes the 5-byte local item_id_table by tile_attr = tile_read_buf[2], the low byte of the +2 ushort terrain_class field, whose range is 0..0x1F. Only classes 0..4 select a defined table entry; classes 5..0x1F read past item_id_table[5] into adjacent stack-frame bytes. In the binary this is the literal frame read *(byte*)((int)&var_14 + var_1a); the emitted C item_id_table[tile_attr] reads whatever Watcom lays out after the 5-byte array, which is frame-layout dependent and not guaranteed bit-identical for out-of-range indices. Already tracked in tools/code_emit/data/emit_issues.json '000354fe' (type frame_layout_oob_index, severity low) and referenced by the source comment. Recording here for refine traceability; NOT fixing in this stage (it is a cut/unreferenced path -- no chapter FDFIELD hook reaches this slot with live tile data, so classes 0..4 are byte-identical and the OOB case is unreachable in real play).

Packs base into BX:CX (high16:low16) and size into SI:DI, sets EAX = 0x601, calls int386(0x31, &in_r, &out_r), and returns 1 when the carry flag is clear (success), 0 otherwise. Functionally identical to fd2_dpmi_lock_region except the DPMI function number is 0x601 (unlock) instead of 0x600 (lock). In the original binary the two share an INT 31h dispatch tail (this body JMPs into fd2_dpmi_lock_region at 0x362a7); the C source models it as a self-contained, functionally-equivalent function.

00036316.purpose: Size-based convenience wrapper that locks a DPMI linear-memory region given a base address and a byte size, by computing end = base + size and delegating to fd2_dpmi_lock_region.
00036316.logic_summary: Tail-wrapper: returns fd2_dpmi_lock_region(base, base + size). EAX (lock_region's CF result) flows straight through to RET.

0004dbb9.purpose: Compute the FD2.SAV integrity checksum by summing all buffer bytes except the trailing 4 (which hold the checksum field itself), returning the natural u32-wrap sum.
0004dbb9.logic_summary: remaining = len - 4; checksum = 0; do { checksum += *pBuf; remaining--; pBuf++; } while (remaining != 0); return checksum. A do-while LODSB/LOOP-style byte sum over the first len-4 bytes. No overflow guard (relies on natural u32 wraparound). do-while means len <= 4 underflows the counter, so callers must pass len > 4 (FD2.SAV uses len = 0x59CB).

0004dbd8.purpose: In-place self-inverse XOR cipher for the FD2.SAV buffer; the identical call encrypts on the write path and decrypts on the read path.
0004dbd8.logic_summary: scramble_state = 0xA5. do { scramble_state = ROL16(scramble_state + 0x9014, 3); *pBuf ^= (byte)scramble_state; pBuf++; len--; } while (len != 0). 16-bit keystream is deterministic from the constant seed, so XOR (self-inverse) makes encrypt and decrypt the same routine. No XOR/keystream/LFSR (immediates are only 0x03/0x04/0xFF/0x1F). The function's own plate and the src comment both explicitly debunk the LFSR/scramble reading as a Ghidra CONCAT11 artifact. Callers confirm intent: fd2_load_chapter_battle_data calls it once after loading FDFIELD tile data to establish a clean transient baseline; AI/pathfind callers (fd2_ai_seek_optimal_position, fd2_ai_walk_to_target_tile, fd2_init_runtime_char_for_battle) call it right after pathfinding/threat-overlay painting to clear the transient occupancy bit (tile_map[idx*4+6] & 0x40, == rec[2] bit 0x40) and movement-range marks. Proposed name follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=battle), accurately describes the reset of per-tile transient/dynamic state, and carries no address residue. Caller plates that say 'decrypt/obfuscate' are stale and out of scope for this symbol.
0004dbfc.purpose: In-place reset of each battle tile record's transient/dynamic fields (occupancy + flag bits, and the rec[3] attribute byte) across the whole tile map, preserving the base terrain byte rec[0].
0004dbfc.logic_summary: Reads tile_count = header[0] (map width) * header[2] (map height) via 8-bit MUL (result fits 16 bits). Advances past the 4-byte header to the first 4-byte tile record, then a do-while over tile_count records: rec[3] = 0xFF; rec[2] &= 0x1F (clears the 0x40 'occupied' bit and 0x80 attribute bit that callers test); rec[1] &= 0x03 (keep low 2 bits); rec[0] untouched; rec += 4. Ghidra renders this as a 16-bit CONCAT11 & 0x1FFF / & 0x3FF >> 8 rolling-state cascade, but that is algebraically identical to the three masks and is a decompiler artifact (each masked byte is freshly loaded, AND-ed, stored; AL=0xFF is loaded once before the loop). No carried state, no encryption.

0004dc34.purpose: Hand-written RLE blit of a 24x24 sprite into dst_buf, recolouring every painted pixel into an 8-colour palette band as ((src_pixel + team_offset) & 7) + color_base.
0004dc34.logic_summary: Outer loop runs 24 rows; per row x_remain starts at 0x18 and is decremented per RLE command until 0, then dst advances by (stride - 0x18) to the next row. Leaf function: no __CHK stack probe, no CALLs.

0004ddd7.logic_summary: Decodes the same 4-mode 24x24 RLE stream as the sibling tile_blit_24x24_* family, one command byte at a time; top two bits select the mode and (low 6 bits + 1) is the run length. RUN (bits 00): skip one ignored source byte, write the fill colour len times contiguously. STRIDE-2 RUN (bits 01): skip one ignored source byte, write colour len times at every other dst byte (dst += 2/pixel). LITERAL (bits 10): consume len ignored source bytes, write colour once each. 0004ea2a.name_reason: Descriptor '_2bpp' is a factual misnomer: the font sheet is 1bpp, not 2bpp. The glyph stride is 0x20 bytes for a 16-row glyph (disasm 0x4eaa0 SHL EAX,0x5 = idx*0x20), i.e. 2 bytes/row = 16 bits over 16 columns = exactly 1 bit per pixel. Each row is read as one byte-swapped ushort (LODSW + XCHG AH,AL at 0x4eac2/0x4eac4) and consumed MSB-first one bit per column (SHL AX,1; JNC at 0x4eac9). The src comment (blitspr.c lines 1149-1152) and the Ghidra plate both already state the sheet is 1bpp and call '2bpp' a misnomer; the name was kept only to stay byte-identical with the live symbol and routing table. Proposed: fd2_blit_glyph_1bpp_with_outline. Recorded only; rename applies in Stage 2 (touches protos.h/types.h/routing.json/dialog.c + 2 call sites in fd2_display_dialog_scene + 6 KB docs).

Step 1: if bg_color != 0, fill a 16x16 box at dst_buf (16 rows x 4 dword writes = 16 bytes/row) with the bg byte replicated to a dword (bg_color*0x01010101), advancing by pitch each row. Step 2: if glyph_idx != 10 (the space glyph; paints nothing but bg fill still runs), set glyph_row = font_data + glyph_idx*0x20 and loop 16 rows: read the row's two bytes as a byte-swapped ushort (first stream byte = left 8 pixels), then for 16 columns test the MSB (sign bit) and shift left; for each set bit write fill_color at the pixel, outline_color at pixel+pitch-1 (shadow below-left) and pixel+pitch (shadow directly below). dst advances by 1 per column, by pitch per row; glyph_row advances by 2 per row. Body wrapped in PUSHAD/POPAD, EAX untouched -> the decompiler 'return in_EAX' is a passthrough artifact; both call sites discard it, so effectively void.

0004eae6.purpose: Bresenham-style nearest-neighbor sprite scaler that paints a scale_num-wide x scale_den-tall output block from an arbitrary src.width x src.height source sprite, skipping transparent (zero) source pixels.

Computes tie_break = caster pCombat_aux_block[0xD] & 0x40 (set forces physical) and shared_raw = caster wAP - best_physical_target wDP. If all three best scores < 6, return 0. Otherwise pick the strict-max category: phys>spell && phys>item -> physical; spell>phys && spell>=item -> spell; item>phys && item>spell -> item. Ties: phys==spell>item -> spell if best_spell_id<0xb and shared_raw<=spell.base_damage(*(uint16*)spell_effect_entry), or if best_spell_id>=0xb and tie_break==0, else physical; phys==item>spell -> item if tie_break==0 else physical; remaining ties fall through to no-op. After dispatch set data_fd2_battle_anim_phase=0 and return 1.

Resolves item_id via fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id and stores it to data_fd2_ui_menu_cursor_idx (active_item_id @0x53C57), then fetches the item effect entry. ctx_flag decides how the small-AOE field pItem[0x11] is used: when ctx_flag==0 pass (small_aoe==0) as flag, else pass small_aoe directly. Branches on range_class=pItem[0x10]: <0x10 short-range -> fd2_compute_aoe_targets with AOE radius pItem[0x12]; >=0x10 long-range -> fd2_scan_chars_along_line_with_team_filter using caster pos and reach range_class-0x10. Finally applies the effect via fd2_apply_use_effect_dispatch(caster, slot, n_targets, target_idxs), clears all-char facing, and zeroes pending_xp_credit. 0001ec2a.purpose: Compute the screen pixel position (x, y) of a combat speech bubble anchored to one runtime char's tile, adjusting for the char's facing direction and clamping so the bubble stays within the 320x200 screen.
0001ec2a.logic_summary: rc = runtime_char_array[char_idx]. Base anchor: out[0]=x=(rc.pos_x - view_window_origin_x)*0x18 + 4; out[1]=y=(rc.pos_y - view_window_origin_y)*0x18. Then branch on facing = rc.sprite_state[1]: if facing < 2 (char faces down/right) place bubble ABOVE the char: new_y = y - 0x12; y = (new_y < 0) ? y+5 : new_y; if right edge overflows (x+0x6C > 0x13F) then x -= 0x56 and return. Else (facing >= 2, char faces up/left) place bubble BELOW: y += (y+0x25 < 200) ? 0x16 : 5; if left edge stays on-screen (x-0x56 >= 0) then x -= 0x58 and return. If neither edge-fix branch returned (bubble would overflow both sides), fall through and nudge x += 0x1C. Void return; results written through out_xy_ptr.

0001ecc7.logic_summary: Indexes data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr by attacker_idx/defender_idx (80-byte runtime_char). Reads AP +0x48, DP +0x4A, HP_cur +0x40, HP_max +0x42, attacker HIT(+0x4C), defender EV(+0x4E), job_id +0x20, level +0x21. Resolves the equipped weapon (fd2_find_equipped_item_by_kind kind=0 -> fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id -> fd2_get_item_effect_entry): weapon_class=entry[9], weapon_elem=entry[10]. Hit roll: RNG, HIT iff rng%100 < (HIT-EV) -> set hit/miss flag=0, RNG crit roll: if rng%100<total_crit white flash and DP/=2; damage=(AP-DP)*9/10 clamped>=0, if damage/9!=0 add RNG%(damage/9) jitter; HP_cur=max(0,HP_cur-damage). Writes HP_cur back to +0x40. XP: only if attacker.team(+6)==TEAM_PLAYER(2) and defender portrait(+7)>=0x44, enemy=fd2_get_enemy_data_entry(portrait-0x44); mid-tier jobs 9..24 or char_id 0x1C add +0x1E to attacker level (divisor); pending_xp=enemy[9]*def_level/atk_level, then if defender survived *damage/HP_max. Leading __CHK(0x58,...) is the Watcom stack/bounds-check CRT intrinsic, not game logic. The Ghidra decompiler mis-folded the RNG return into the crit variable in 4 spots; the assembly-true predicates are rng%100<weapon_elem (poison hit), rng%4+2 (poison duration, NOT (rng/4)%4), rng%100<(HIT-EV) (hit), rng%100<total_crit (crit), rng%(damage/9) (jitter).

00025052.purpose: Additive over-bright palette pulse: walk intensity from start_intensity down to 0 inclusive, re-applying the full DAC range each step (with a per-step delay), so the screen white-flashes then settles back to the base palette.
00025052.logic_summary: for (intensity = (int)start_intensity; intensity >= 0; intensity--) { fd2_set_vga_palette_range_with_add(0, 0xFF, intensity); fd2_delay_ms(step_delay_ms); }. 00025bf4.name_reason: This is literally the C entry point that the Watcom CRT startup (__CMain @ 0x45D4B) calls via main(argc, argv) and whose EAX it consumes as the DOS exit code. 00025bf4.purpose: FD2 game C entry point: performs one-shot startup (AIL sound init, resource loads, work-buffer mallocs, mode-13h set, RNG warm-up) then runs the outer main-menu / inner gameplay loop until quit, finally tearing down sound and restoring text video mode.
00025bf4.logic_summary: One-shot init: AIL_startup; install MDI (BGM) driver and, if present, set available flag + allocate sequence handle; install DIG (SFX) driver and, if present, set available flag + allocate two sample handles. Eight fd2_load_dat_resource loads from FDOTHER.DAT (indices 0x1F,1,2,3,4,5,6) plus one FDTXT.DAT (index 0), each passing the prior pointer so the loader frees-then-reloads. Three work-buffer mallocs (0x20 tile-event flags, 0x25680 large state buffer, 0xA00 menu roster). Set INT 10h AX=0x0013 (VGA mode 13h) via int386 over the shared REGS union. Latch BIOS tick word [0x46C] into the ambient-palette timer. RNG warm-up: advance fd2_advance_rng_state() rand()%256 times (under FD2_REPLAY the warm-up count is forced to 0 for determinism). Outer loop: set main-menu BGM (track 0x12) and call fd2_main_menu_continue_dispatcher; if it returns 0, run the inner gameplay loop: fd2_game_main_loop, then branch on data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (@0x53ECC): ==1 -> play chapter-clear fanfare; ==2 -> run the current chapter's end handler, present the chapter-transition menu, and on continue run the next chapter's init handler + set its turn BGM (otherwise request quit); both reset the end-code and toggle the play-active flag. -1 results request quit. On quit: AIL_shutdown, set INT 10h AX=0x0003 (text mode 3), return.

00025ebb.logic_summary: Calls fd2_play_ending_and_record_clear() and switches on its EAX return (menu_choice). (A) choice==0 NEW GAME: fade to black, current_chapter_id=0, reload FDOTHER[0] palette, reset menu_party_member_count, clear play-active flag, invoke chapter_init_handler_table[0] (chapter 01 init), set chapter-0 player-turn BGM, re-arm play-active flag, clear keyboard; returns 0. (B) choice==1 CONTINUE: load FDOTHER[0xD] intro atlas + FDOTHER[0] palette, clear VGA framebuffer, malloc 0x59CB save buffer, read+decrypt FD2.SAV (or fill 0xFF if absent), then a do/while save-slot selector loop calling fd2_save_slot_selector_ui; for a chosen slot it memmoves the 0xA00 roster block and restores chapter id / party count / gold / hud+speed+audio flags from the per-slot state at +0x312B (an all-0xFF empty slot resets slot_result=0 to re-prompt). After freeing buffers, if a slot was committed (slot_result==1) it clears play-active, calls fd2_chapter_transition_menu() (reassigning slot_result), and on its 0 result runs the chapter init handler + sets that chapter's BGM; returns the (reassigned) slot_result. (C) else (incl. choice==2): mute BGM (-1), call fd2_load_save_and_init_engine() for a full engine reload, set the loaded chapter's BGM; returns 0. The leading PUSH 0x20 / CALL 0x36cd7 is a Watcom __CHK stack-probe (no logic).

returns.semantics: Dispatch code for fd2_main's outer loop, with semantics INVERTED relative to the branch labels: 0 = run gameplay this iteration then re-show the menu (returned by NEW GAME, by fallback, and by CONTINUE after a committed slot whose chapter-transition returns 0); 1 = quit the game (terminates fd2_main's do/while outer loop); -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) = stay in / re-enter the main menu next iteration (CONTINUE when the slot selector / chapter-transition backs out). Confirmed by caller fd2_main: return 0 enters the inner gameplay loop; return 0xFFFFFFFF is mapped to 0 to re-loop the menu; return 1 falls through 'while (menu_result==0)' to AIL_shutdown.

000286bd.purpose: Linearly interpolate a contiguous VGA palette range [start_idx, end_idx) between the stored base palette (data_fd2_vga_palette_data_ptr) and a target color (R,G,B), writing the blended result straight to the Mode-13h DAC.

Target components are masked to 8 bits (MOVZX). cdecl, void; EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP callee-saved.

It calls fd2_load_dat_resource("FDOTHER.DAT"=0x51A4D, 0, fdother_idx) and returns its pointer. Source reproduces the bounded 8-byte local + memcpy-of-6 + 1-based index 1:1 so the binary's buffer/indexing behavior is preserved exactly. Disasm verified: PUSH 0x20;CALL __CHK; SUB ESP,8; MOV EAX,[ESP+0x14]; MOV ESI,0x525d6;MOVSD;MOVSW; TEST EAX,EAX;JZ; CMP byte[EAX+4],0;JZ; MOVZX EAX,byte[EAX+4]; MOVZX EAX,byte[ESP+EAX-1]; PUSH EAX;PUSH 0;PUSH 0x51a4d;CALL fd2_load_dat_resource;ADD ESP,0xC; RET.

Canonical envelope sets 0 before and 1 after fd2_run_full_turn_cycle; fd2_set_battle_anim_phase_to_1 is the dedicated '=1' setter. Widely written by chapter NN init/end handlers (cutscene phase markers, reset to 0 after dialog pages), AI turn logic, menu/dialog loops, and spell effects.

Two dispatch idioms: (1) primary battle path -- AI/turn loops set data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_idx @ 0x51A8F (0xFF = none) and, if != 0xFF on the next iteration, call table[idx](char_idx) (counter/death/status proc), resetting the latch to 0xFF; (2) direct path -- fd2_handle_tile_event_interaction (field-map event tile, entry type 'other'), fd2_fire_chapter_turn_events_for_phase (turn-gated chapter scripts, entry .event_id), and fd2_process_battle_drop_entries (kill-drop entry type 2) load the table base with a literal [idx*4 + 0x51B91] (these are the only three xrefs Ghidra reports). Several 'unref_*' slots have no reachable in-game event id but are emitted verbatim to preserve the 90-entry shape.

00051b91.element_semantics: Each element is a 32-bit code pointer to a chapter-event handler fd2_chapter_event_handler_NN__* with ABI void(uint32 char_idx) (single cdecl dword arg = active character/recipient index).

00014237.name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=ai, descriptor=score_physical_attack). Accurately reflects purpose (enemy AI scores physical-attack candidates and records the best). No Ghidra address residue, no domain-ID stripping needed.
00014237.purpose: Enemy AI: evaluate every reachable tile for a physical attack with the caster's equipped weapon and record the single best candidate (target tile x/y, target runtime_char index, score class) into the ai_best_physical_* result globals.
00014237.logic_summary: Init best tiebreak=0, ai_best_physical_score=0. Read attacker AP/DP. Find equipped weapon (kind 0); if none, return 0. Read weapon AoE shape (x@+0xB, y@+0xC). Movement class = 0x13 when status-immunity predicate holds for caster, else job byte @+0x20. Get move-cost table; malloc pAlloc_a(0x20, allocated/freed but content unused), pTile_pos_buf(0x800). ctx_flag==0 -> use_smaller_aoe=1. Paint threat overlay, flood-fill movement range, mark friendly-occupant tiles, collect unmarked reachable tiles -> n_reachable, re-obfuscate tile map. malloc pTarget_id_buf(100). For each reachable candidate tile: effective AP/DP = base + (terrain_mv/def_modifier[tile_id] * stat)/100, applied only when status-immunity predicate holds (tile_id = tile_buf[5] from fd2_read_tile_attribute_at_pos). Compute AoE targets at candidate; re-obfuscate. For each AoE target: target AP/DP with same terrain adjustment; raw_dmg = effective_AP - target_DP; score_class = 0 if raw_dmg<=2 else 8; if raw_dmg > target.HP_current -> raw_dmg*=2, score_class=0x12 (kill). If target can default-attack back (==1) -> raw_dmg += effective_DP - target_AP (counter bonus). If target.char_id==0 (party leader) -> raw_dmg = raw_dmg*3/2. Keep candidate when score_class > best, or (== best && raw_dmg > tiebreak): store cand_x/cand_y/target_idx/score_class and tiebreak. Free 3 buffers, return 0.

0001567e.purpose: Enemy AI item-use evaluator: scans every usable inventory item across every reachable target tile and records the single best item-use candidate into the ai_best_item_* result globals.
0001567e.logic_summary: Resets ai_best_item_score to 0 and pre-loads the job-0 movement-cost table (side-effect: sets the cost-table globals). Reads caster tile (x,y) and mallocs a 400-byte tile-position buffer. n_slots = fd2_count_usable_inventory_slots(caster). For each usable slot: item_id = caster.inventory_slots[slot].item_id; pItem = fd2_get_item_effect_entry(item_id). Skip non-offensive items (pItem[0xD]==0). range_class=pItem[0x10]; a range_class>0x0F (long-range projectile) is clamped to 1 for the reachability precompute. Flood the caster's reachable area via fd2_compute_aoe_targets at the caster pos, collect unmarked tiles into the buffer (n_reachable), then de-obfuscate the tile map. For each reachable tile (cx,cy): pick aoe_arg -- when ctx_flag==0 use (pItem[0x11]==0?1:0), else use pItem[0x11]. If short-range (pItem[0x10]<0x10): n_targets = fd2_compute_aoe_targets(cx,cy,tgt_buf,pItem[0x12],0,aoe_arg); else (long-range): n_targets = fd2_scan_chars_along_line_with_team_filter(cx,cy,tgt_buf,caster_x,caster_y,pItem[0x10]-0x10,0). De-obfuscate tile map. If n_targets>0: score = fd2_score_item_candidate(item_id,n_targets,tgt_buf); if score > ai_best_item_score, update score/target_x/target_y/slot. Finally free the buffer. Underlying routine returns 0 (unused; src declares void).

00015880.purpose: Per-candidate offensive-item scorer for enemy AI: given one item and a list of target char-indices, returns the summed priority score over those targets, used by fd2_ai_score_item_use to compare (item, tile) candidates.
00015880.logic_summary: total=0. pItem = fd2_get_item_effect_entry(item_id); spell_or_damage = *(uint16*)(pItem+0xE); effect_code = pItem[0xD]. Dispatch: (A) effect_code==5||0xD (HP-damage item): for each target_id in target_array_ptr[0..n_targets): pChar = runtime_char_array + target_id*0x50; hp=*(uint16*)(pChar+0x40); hp_max=*(uint16*)(pChar+0x42); per_score = (hp<=hp_max/3)?8 : (hp>hp_max/2)?0 : 3; if (pChar[0x34] & 0x80) per_score*=3; total+=per_score. (B) effect_code==0x14||0x15||0x18 (spell-wrapper item): pSpell = fd2_get_spell_effect_entry(spell_or_damage); if (effect_code!=0x18) spell_or_damage = *(uint16*)pSpell (spell base damage; for 0x18 keep item[0xE] as threshold); for each target: hp=*(uint16*)(pChar+0x40); per_score = (spell_or_damage>=hp)?0x12 : 8; total+=per_score. 0001598a.purpose: Enemy AI offensive-spell planner: scores every castable spell x every reachable cast tile and writes the single best candidate (score, target tile, spell id) into the ai_best_spell_* globals.
0001598a.logic_summary: Resets ai_best_spell_score to 0 and preloads the job-0 movement-cost table. Frees the tile buffer; returns 0 (declared void in src).

00029c90.purpose: BG zoom-in scroll transition for a combat cinematic: camera pushes in toward a combat unit by scrolling a 3-layer parallax background down then up, compositing the unit pose into the work buffer between the two passes.

Phase 3: for frame_iter 9..0, RLE-blit special_attack_bg_layer[(frame_iter+2)%3] into workspace+0x140 (rotated layer cycle), then blit the offset band to mode-13h, giving an upward scroll. The 3 BG-layer pointers are read directly from the real uint32[3] array data_fd2_battle_special_cinematic_bg_layers @ 0x5410B/0F/13.

0002a2e8.purpose: Plays the full-screen CLASS PROMOTION cinematic: the promoting member's silhouette morphs into the target-class silhouette over a 3-layer parallax BG with an additive shine flash.
0002a2e8.logic_summary: Loads 3 parallax BGs from BG.DAT[0..2] into data_fd2_battle_special_cinematic_bg_layers[0..2], loads the caster silhouette FIGANI.DAT[caster.portrait_id*3] and target-class silhouette FIGANI.DAT[class_id*3], backs up the current VGA frame (memmove from 0xA0000). Phase 2: cycle_sprite_anim_with_bg_frames(caster, work, 0x10) = 16 anim frames. Phase 3: 20-step additive palette flash (set_vga_palette_range_with_add iter*3, 10ms/step). Phase 4: clear work, blit target silhouette at slide-in cap (flash_iter*10 = 0x14*10), restore full brightness, cycle_sprite_anim_with_bg_frames(target, work, 0x18) = 24 frames. Phase 5: fade to black, restore pre-cinematic VGA frame, fade in, free all buffers. The 3 BG-layer pointers are a real uint32[3] array indexed directly for ascending-adjacency guarantee. A dead BIOS-tick read (MOV EAX,0x46C; MOVSX) before the Phase-1 JZ has no effect and is not reproduced (the JZ tests ADD ESP,0xC flags, never taken, so the cycler advances every frame).

0002a5d0.purpose: Generic sprite-animation player loop: renders iter_count frames of an indexed-sprite atlas over a 3-variant cycling parallax background, one BIOS tick per frame, advancing the atlas frame according to its own per-frame hold counts.
0002a5d0.logic_summary: Loop iter (0..iter_count-1). Each iteration: memset(workspace,0,0x1F400); bg_variant_idx=(bg_variant_idx+1)%3 (advances unconditionally every frame); rle-blit data_fd2_battle_special_cinematic_bg_layers[bg_variant_idx] at y=0x32 into workspace (stride 0x280, key -1); blit current atlas frame_idx into workspace; blit_rectangle workspace -> VGA aperture 0xA0000 (0x140x0xC8). Then per-frame hold: hold_count = byte at (sprite_atlas + 6 + *(int*)(sprite_atlas + 8 + frame_idx*4)) (atlas-relative: [8+frame_idx*4] is the per-frame block offset, +6 within that block holds the hold count); tick++; when tick==hold_count, reset tick to 0 via XOR-with-self and frame_idx++, wrapping frame_idx to 0 (XOR-with-self) when it reaches frame_count = *(byte*)sprite_atlas (atlas[0]). Finally fd2_wait_n_bios_ticks(1). Note the leading __CHK(0x34,...) stack-probe call emitted by the compiler.

Inline: (1) copy 6 .rodata const tables to stack (shake X/Y offsets, HP-lerp hit counts, player/enemy team caster sprite-id tables, intro SFX-bank table), set palette_op_base/shine_table_offset from spell_id; (2) free portrait_sprite_cache/large_game_state_buffer/battle_scene_snapshot, zero the 30-dword FIGANI stack buffer; (3) resolve bg_idx/tai_idx from per-chapter cinematic-mode override (chapter_combat_cinematic_mode_per_chapter[current_chapter]) or the tile attr byte, swapped by caster.team, plus fd2_resolve_terrain_for_aoe_targets; (4) load BG.DAT[bg_idx], TAI.DAT[tai_idx], caster FIGANI (portrait*3 and +2, falling back to +1 if first int16==0), FDOTHER spell SFX bank, per-target FIGANI, team caster sprite; (5) malloc 64000 backbuffer + 0x2A300 frame-scratch, stamp caster; (6) intro zoom + figani loop; (7) optional spell_id==9 slide-in, then cinematic phases via FF/4 indirect through data_fd2_battle_spell_cast_cinematic_phase_handler_table[spell_id] (5 args caster_idx/team_caster_sprite/work_buf/stride/phase_code, returns this phase's frame count); (8) per-target main loop: snapshot tgt HP, damage=fd2_calc_magic_damage (writes HP, 0=miss via SETZ), restore snapshot, lerp HP bar over hit_count steps toward post-damage value, hit shows shake/flash pose + advances shake state (shake_y_dir=1-(rng%3) from fd2_advance_rng_state EAX) while miss shows the 'miss' frame; (9) post-cast phase-6 loop + spell_id==9 slide-out + final 3-frame shake/shine lerp; (10) free all resources, reallocate large_game_state_buffer (0x25680), reload battle_scene_snapshot from FDSHAP.DAT[tile_event_data[0]*2], restore portrait cache, fade out, clear VGA, composite, fade in.

Blit tile 0 from the runtime_battle_state atlas (atlas base = pointer value data_fd2_runtime_battle_state_ptr) at the player-row slot reserved_char_pos: (reserved_char_pos*0x19+0x56, 0x84) as a highlight overlay. 7. memmove(0xA0000, dst, 64000); free(dst). Every tile draw goes through fd2_blit_24x24_tile_to_battle_grid_position(atlas_base, tile_id, dst_buf, stride=0x140, dst_x, dst_y).

00036107.name_reason: The trailing _36107 equals the function's own address (0x00036107), i.e. a Ghidra address residue, not a domain ID. 00036107.purpose: Mode-flag-dispatched chunk fetcher for the LX module-loader pipeline: copies 'length' bytes into dest either by file read (lseek+read) or in-memory copy (memcpy), selected by mode bit0, and returns the chunk's end position for chained reads.
00036107.logic_summary: Computes the return value end = offset + length up front (EBX in the original, before any callee CALL, so it is independent of the helpers' return values). If (mode & 1) == 0: lseek(file_handle, offset, SEEK_SET) then read(file_handle, dest, length) -- file-backed path. Else (bit0 set): memcpy(dest, (void*)(file_handle + offset), length) -- in-memory path, with file_handle reused as a base address. Returns offset + length. cyclomatic complexity 2; callees memcpy(0x3cbd6), lseek(0x3cc00), read(0x3cc4b).
00036107.signature: int __cdecl crt_equivalent_lx_chunk_read_36107(int file_handle, int offset, byte mode, void *dest, uint length)

params.name: file_handle
params.semantics: In file mode (bit0 clear) this is the OS file descriptor passed to lseek/read. In memory mode (bit0 set) it is reused as a base address, and memcpy reads from file_handle+offset. The name reflects the primary (file) role; the dual use is documented in the comment.
params.reason: Accurately names the file-mode role (the common path through callers); dual base-address use is explained in the comment. No address residue.

params.name: offset
params.semantics: File seek position (SEEK_SET) in file mode, or byte offset added to the base address in memory mode. Also one of the two addends of the returned end position (offset+length).
params.reason: Correct and generic for both dispatch paths; no address residue.

params.name: mode
params.semantics: Dispatch flag; only bit0 is tested. bit0 clear => file read; bit0 set => in-memory memcpy. Forwarded verbatim by the LX header reader / module loader so every chunk read selects the same backing store.
params.reason: Describes the byte's role as a mode selector; no address residue.

params.name: dest
params.semantics: Destination buffer that receives the 'length' fetched bytes (target of read or memcpy).
params.reason: Clear and correct; no address residue.

params.name: length
params.semantics: Number of bytes to fetch (count for read/memcpy) and the second addend of the returned end position (offset+length).
params.reason: Correct byte-count name; no address residue.

returns.semantics: End position of the chunk = offset + length. Computed before any helper CALL, so it is unaffected by lseek/read/memcpy return values. Callers chain it as the next read's starting offset (e.g. obj_tbl_off = chunk_read(... )) to walk consecutive object-table / page-table / fixup records.

0003615e.purpose: Install a new AIL internal allocator function pointer (data_ail_alloc_fnptr at 0x52758) and return the previous one, so a caller can save/restore or compare it.

returns.semantics: The previous value of data_ail_alloc_fnptr (the allocator function pointer in effect before this call), returned in EAX. Lets the caller restore or compare the old allocator.

00036344.name_reason: Prefix crt_equivalent_ is correct (FD2-customized CRT-equivalent LX loader helper, not a vendor byte-match). The _36344 suffix is Ghidra address residue: it equals the function's own entry address 0x36344 (same class as the _52758 residue called out in the rules). The descriptor lx_header_reader is unique in the CRT pool, so stripping the address suffix is safe and required. Descriptor accurately reflects the body: it reads/introspects the MZ->LX header and object table.
00036344.purpose: LX/LE executable header introspection: validate MZ->LX wiring and compute an FD2-specific image-size aggregate (num_objects*15 + sum of object virtual sizes) used by the LX module loader to size its output buffer.
00036344.logic_summary: Pre-fills a 4-byte magic slot with 0x00002020 (loaded from the relocated immediate at 0x360ff). Resolves a handle: if mode_byte&1==0 it open()s path with oflag 0x200 (returns 0 on -1); if mode_byte&1==1 it reuses arg0 directly as an in-memory base address. Reads 4-byte e_lfanew at MZ+0x3C (no MZ-magic check), reads the 2-byte LX magic at e_lfanew into the slot, and strcmp()s the slot against "LX" (data at 0x502f0). On magic mismatch it calls close(handle) UNCONDITIONALLY (ignores mode bit0) and returns 0. On match it re-reads the full 0xAC LX header into a stack buffer, computes obj_tbl_off = e_lfanew + lx_header[+0x40] (object_table_offset) and num_objects = lx_header[+0x44], then loops num_objects times reading each 0x18-byte object record (chaining obj_tbl_off through the chunk reader's returned end position) and accumulates record[+0x00] (object virtual size). It close()s the handle only when mode bit0 is clear, and returns num_objects*15 + accumulated virtual size (SHL 4 / SUB pattern = *15). All file/memory access is delegated to crt_equivalent_lx_chunk_read_36107, which selects lseek+read vs memcpy based on the same mode bit0.

params.name: path
params.semantics: Overloaded by mode_byte bit0. When bit0==0 it is a null-terminated path string that is open()ed. When bit0==1 it is an int reused as an in-memory base address (every chunk read becomes memcpy from base+offset; open/close skipped). Forwarded to the chunk reader as the file_handle/base argument.
params.reason: The name path only covers the bit0-clear case. In bit0-set mode arg0 is an in-memory base address (see callee memcpy(dest, offset+file_handle, length)), not a path. path_or_base captures both roles without an address suffix.

params.name: mode_byte
params.semantics: Mode/store-selector. bit0: 0 => file-backed (open path, lseek+read, close at end); 1 => in-memory (arg0 is a base address, memcpy, skip open/close). Forwarded verbatim to every crt_equivalent_lx_chunk_read_36107 call so the same backing store is used for each read.
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate; no address residue. Captures the mode/flag nature of the byte.

returns.semantics: FD2-specific image-size aggregate = num_objects*15 + sum(object virtual_size) on a valid LX module; 0 on open failure (-1) or LX magic mismatch. Not a standard loader-API value; consumed by crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader_3647b as the total_size for buffer allocation/memset.

reads_globals: 0x360ff (relocated immediate 0x00002020 used to pre-fill the LX magic slot)

issues.title: Unconditional close(handle) on LX magic mismatch ignores mode bit0
issues.description: On LX magic mismatch the function calls close(handle) without testing mode_byte&1. When called in in-memory mode (bit0==1), arg0 is a base address rather than a real file descriptor, so close() is invoked on a non-handle value. This is faithfully reproduced from the original binary (disassembly 0x363ea: PUSH EBP; CALL close at 0x3d01c is unconditional) and MUST NOT be changed -- the CRT-equivalent logic is verified to match FD2.LE. Recorded for awareness only. Practically unreachable: the sole (itself-dead) caller crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader_3647b only loads a valid LE image. The success-path close() at the end is correctly gated by bit0; only the mismatch error path is not.
issues.evidence: disassemble_function 0x00036344: at 0x363e8 JZ skips to 0x363f5 (match path); fall-through 0x363ea PUSH EBP / 0x363eb CALL 0x0003d01c (close) then JMP 0x3638a (return 0), with no TEST of [ESP+0xe0]&1 guarding it -- contrast the success-path close at 0x36451 TEST byte ptr [ESP+0xe0],0x1 / JNZ 0x36464.

Verified pre-fill value 0x00002020 by reading memory at 0x360ff (bytes 20 20 00 00) and strcmp target by reading 0x502f0 (bytes 4c 58 00 00 = "LX"). Return *15 confirmed via SHL EAX,0x4 / SUB EAX,EDX at 0x3646a-0x3646d. __cdecl confirmed: plain RET at 0x3647a, sole caller cleans 2 args (ADD ESP,0x8). Name/param renames recorded only; to be applied in Stage 2 (touches protos.h + the single call site at 0x364cc in crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader_3647b).

However, the entire CRT-equivalent LX family in src/crt/crt.c uses the same address-tag convention as a stable disambiguator (crt_equivalent_lx_chunk_read_36107 @0x36107, crt_equivalent_lx_header_reader_36344 @0x36344, crt_equivalent_exit_chain_stub_36de3 @0x36de3); renaming this one in isolation would break the family's uniform naming and these siblings are referenced by call site inside this very body. Marked uncertain rather than rename so Stage 2 makes the family-wide call.

Reverses the shard's keep lean (which assumed the family kept the tag): ALL 6 other crt_equivalent_* address-tagged fns (lx_chunk_read_36107, lx_header_reader_36344, exit_chain_stub_36de3, fpe_default_handler_3d26e, matherr_default_thunk_4d340, matherr_default_return_zero_4d8ea) have verdict=rename dropping the tag, so keeping _3647b would make this the lone address-tagged outlier. Family policy = drop the tag. Descriptor unique after drop.
0003647b.purpose: Watcom CRT-equivalent LX/LE runtime module loader: reads the MZ->LX header, walks the object + page + fixup tables, writes the loaded image into a caller buffer (or a freshly allocated one) and applies 32-bit relocations. Dead in FD2 (static-link single-LE never invokes runtime LE loading) but re-emitted because the CLIB3S overlay/dynamic-load chain pulls in the __loadm-family obj and this body does not byte-match the public Watcom one.
0003647b.logic_summary: 1) handle = (flags&1)?path-as-handle : open(path,0x200); open==-1 -> return 0. 2) total_size = crt_equivalent_lx_header_reader_36344(path,flags). 3) if flags&4: caller_buf = (*data_ail_alloc_fnptr)(total_size); null -> close(if !flags&1)+return 0; else use caller_buf. 4) memset(caller_buf,0,total_size); out_cursor=alloc_base=caller_buf. 5) read e_lfanew (MZ+0x3C, 4B) + 2B magic; strcmp vs "LX"; mismatch -> close+return 0. 6) read full 0xAC LX header into lx_header. 7) for each object (lx_header+0x44 count): read 0x18 object record; for each page (obj+0x10 count): read 0x8 page entry; on first page of a flag-3 (bit0|bit1) object with a misaligned cursor and obj_idx!=0, bump out_cursor by 0x10-(alloc_base&0xf) for 16-byte inter-object alignment; record obj_base_table[obj_idx+1]=out_cursor and page_base_table[page_count]=out_cursor; read min(obj_remaining, page byte-count) bytes from (page_data_idx<<shift)+page_data_base into out_cursor; advance out_cursor. 8) read first cumulative fixup-page offset (lx_header+0x68). 9) for each fixup page (lx_header+0x14 count): read next cumulative offset; for each fixup record in [prev,this): read src_type+target_type, validate ((src_type&7)!=0 && !((target_type&4)&&!(target_type&0x20)) && !(src_type&0x20)) else abort->close->return 0; read src_offset(2)+target_obj(1)+target_disp(2); if src_offset<=lx_header+0x28 write obj_base_table[target_obj]+target_disp at page_base_table[page]+src_offset (32-bit reloc). 10) close handle (if !flags&1); return caller_buf.

params.name: path
params.semantics: Overloaded by flags bit0: when flags&1==0 it is a null-terminated path string passed to open(); when flags&1==1 it is a caller-supplied int handle reused as an in-memory base (each chunk read becomes a memcpy). Also forwarded verbatim to crt_equivalent_lx_header_reader_36344.
params.reason: Name reflects the documented dominant role (path to open). The flags&1 handle-overload is fully documented in the comment block, so 'path' remains the clearest primary label; no address residue.

params.name: flags
params.semantics: Bit-flags controlling load mode: bit0 = use-caller-handle (skip open/close, treat path as handle), bit2 = allocate the output buffer via data_ail_alloc_fnptr (else use caller_buf). Low byte also passed to the header reader and every chunk read.
params.reason: Accurate, generic, no address residue.

params.name: caller_buf

0004e0dc.purpose: Recursive 4-neighbour flood fill that paints the movement-range residual-cost markers ('where can this unit move?') across the battle tile map; reached only via the orchestrator fd2_init_movement_range_floodfill and self-recursion.
0004e0dc.logic_summary: For each of the four directions in the binary's fixed order right/left/down/up: bounds-check the neighbour (right/down use unsigned (coord+1)<extent; left/up require coord!=0), then call fd2_flood_fill_neighbor_step(cost, neighbour_btm, &new_cost) which conditionally writes the neighbour's marker and returns non-zero (binary carry-clear) iff the tile improved, leaving the reduced residual in new_cost; on a non-zero return, recurse into that neighbour with new_cost. The current x/y/cost/btm_ptr persist unchanged across all four directions and across each recursive call so every direction starts from the same residual. Termination: when cost-tile_cost underflows or no longer improves the existing marker. In FD2.LE this used the Watcom register-passing convention (DL=x, DH=y, CL=cost, EBX=marker ptr, EBP=map_width*4 stride, ESI=cost-table base) with a hand-rolled 7-byte {x,y,cost,btm_ptr} recursion frame walked via EDI at the pathfind step-stack workspace; the emit replaces that with native C recursion + parameters and recomputes the row stride (map_width*4) from the map_width global. Layer-2 equivalent: identical marker writes, visit order, and termination.

The '_106' suffix is the array dimension (106 entries = event_id 0..105), NOT a Ghidra address residue: 0x627D8 has no relation to 106, and 106 == 0x6A == the documented event_id count and the declared [106] size. Per the naming rule, dimension counts are meaningful domain values and must be preserved. Keep.
000627d8.purpose: Per-chapter cutscene / walk-animation event script pointer table; indexed by event_id (0..105) to obtain the pointer to that event's walk-animation byte-script.
000627d8.logic_summary: Sole reader fd2_get_cutscene_event_script(event_id) returns table[event_id] (disasm: MOV EAX,[event_id*4 + 0x627D8]). The returned pointer is then walked byte-by-byte by fd2_cutscene_event_trigger as a walk-animation byte-script ([n_groups][group: walk_count_or_flags | step_count | {char_idx,dir}*step_count]+, 3 modes by walk_count_or_flags bit7). All 106 entries point into one contiguous byte-stream block stored immediately after the table in .object3 (0x62980..0x634D1, 2898 bytes, = end of .object3). Source emits the byte-stream block (static cutscene_event_script_data[2898]) plus this table referencing offsets into it (Layer-2-equivalent).
000627d8.element_semantics: Each element is a const uint8 * pointing into the contiguous cutscene-event byte-stream; element[event_id] is the start of that event's walk-animation script, consumed byte-by-byte (every consumer reads bytes, so element type is byte-pointer).
